periods.summary: Stella watches Shizuku's match, supports her rival from the stands, and later secretly continues her romance with Ikki. During the Okutama investigation she catches a severe summer cold, is cared for by Ikki in a mountain hut, and discusses intimacy, marriage order, and meeting each other's parents. The leaked kiss photo turns her relationship into a manufactured scandal; she briefly blames herself and considers separation, but Shizuku violently reminds her that Ikki is defending their love. Stella then resolves to fight in her own way: she wins her final selection battle in three seconds, arrives in time to encourage Ikki, and after his victory accepts his proposal. When Akaza tries to interfere, she casually knocks him away while carrying Ikki to treatment.

Ouma's Kusanagi overpowers her Calusaritio Salamander, and Toka knocks Stella unconscious to preserve her as a Seven Stars representative. The defeat leaves Stella anguished by the pain of being weak, so she asks Nene for a week of hellish training before the tournament.

periods.summary: Stella is absent from the pre-tournament banquet because she continues intensive training with Nene Saikyo after being defeated by Ouma. A train delay caused by a rockslide makes her miss her original match start, but the committee postpones the bout. After Ikki defeats Moroboshi, Stella arrives openly confident, apologizes for being late, and voluntarily accepts punishment. Her true aim is not mere royal honesty: she refuses to let Akatsuki's B-block members avoid fighting each other and escape unscathed after the attack on Hagun. She therefore proposes that Mikoto Tsuruya, Reisen Hiraga, Rinna Kazamatsuri and Yui Tatara all fight her at once.

periods.summary: Stella turns her delayed first match into an unprecedented four-on-one B-block special match so Akatsuki representatives cannot avoid facing her. She first measures her enemies' strength to avoid killing them, then defeats Yui Tatara by smashing through Complete Reflection despite losing the use of her left hand. She overcomes Mikoto Tsuruya's absolute-zero eye, Rinna's beasts, and Charlotte Corday's extraordinary shields, even welding her own broken arm with flame so she can use both hands again. When Reisen Hiraga uses a controlled Mikoto as a hostage, Stella discards her sword out of contempt and uses Brute Soul/Brute Dragon Roar in fantasy form, relying on the arena staff and Ouma's wind wall to contain it. The blast annihilates the arena and Hiraga's puppet body, leaves Stella the sole standing fighter, and causes B-block's remaining matches to collapse, sending her directly to the semifinals. Later she reunites with Ikki at the hotel, struggles with guilt about the compressed schedule, and regains confidence when Ikki frames their earlier final as a gift.

periods.summary: Stella's vol-08 side stories emphasize the awkwardness and sincerity of her love for Ikki. She is tricked into playing an otome game with an Ikki-like character and is overheard shouting a marriage line. After Ikki's post-Toka coma, Shizuku tests her as Ikki's partner; Stella cleans a room within a harsh limit using fire, salvages a sabotaged dish into vegetable croquettes, and answers that she will love Ikki and make him happy. She later spares Shizuku the burden of formally conceding, inviting continued rivalry instead. During the student-council ghost hunt she is terrified of ghosts despite being fearless in battle. During Nene's training she cannot sleep without Ikki's presence and resorts to smelling a swapped sheet, revealing both dependence and comic obsession.

periods.summary: Stella watches over Ikki after the Byakuya match and catches Sara trying to undress him in the infirmary, leading to a slapstick struggle with bandages. She meets Ikki's father Itsuki for the first time, is mortified by her awkward greeting, then erupts in anger when he proposes severing ties with Ikki. Because Sara's damaged outfit could distract Ikki's match, Stella drags her shopping with Ikki, Shizuku and Alice, suffers comic insecurity about Sara's figure, and is tricked by Shizuku into presenting herself to Ikki as a bunny girl. She rescues a teleporting infant in a department-store restroom and sees Sara's unexpected maternal side. In the evening Stella alone applauds Ouma after his brutal win over Renji, interpreting his lethal thoroughness as respect for a worthy fighter, and declares she will force him to take her seriously in the semifinal. She watches Ikki's match with Rinna and Charlotte, first trusting him absolutely and then trembling when she realizes he survived the copied Edelweiss by intentionally using his skull to slow the blade. Ikki's win renews her desire to meet him in the final.

periods.summary: Stella crashes into the waiting room and silences Amane when he tries to publicly defile Shizuku's feelings, warning that she will burn him if he continues. That night she reassures Ikki, demonstrates the raw strength gained from Nene's training, and promises to reach the final first. In the semifinal against Ouma, she begins with overwhelming fire and swordplay but cannot cut his steel-like body. Ouma explains his self-imposed Tianlong armor training and overpowers her until she awakens her true power: she is not merely a fire user but a concept-interference Blazer manifesting the mythic Dragon. Dragon Spirit grants her enormous strength, inner heat, and regenerative toughness. She defeats Ouma's Tenryu armor and final Dan Getsu Tenryu Claw with her greatest flame sword, wins the first semifinal, and retains respect for Ouma's unbroken will. When Ikki collapses and wakes after the scheduled final day, Stella has waited in the arena all day with the crowd. She asks for his real feelings, not an apology, and helps trigger the committee's rescheduling of their final.

key_events.summary: Protects Shizuku from Amane's public verbal violation.
Flashback reveals Nene forced her to awaken Dragon Spirit.
Defeats Ouma after revealing her true dragon concept.
Waits all day for Ikki and has the final rescheduled.
